requirements.title: A recorded answer is written down as a rule
requirements.rationale: A decision the person asks to keep must reach the repository, where later sessions read it, and must change nothing else on the way.

criteria.condition: the event `decision.answered` is appended, or nightshiftd starts, and a decision of a kind other than `rule` is answered with `record: true` and has no rule yet
criteria.action: store one rule for the decision in the state `writing`, with the decision's id, its workspace, its thread, its question, the answered option and the comment
criteria.contract: exactly one rule exists per decision id, also when the event is seen twice or nightshiftd stopped between the answer and the event; the rule reads back as {decision, workspace, thread, question, option, comment, state: `writing`}

setup: a rule service over a copy of the store template, an inbox with a test decision kind `test` (options `yes`, `no`), the fake hub (internal/hubtest) and a fake of the scheduler's RunSession that the test scripts
check.pseudocode: new file internal/rule/rule_test.go, a table over {an answer with record true -> one rule with the decision's question, option and comment; the same decision.answered event handled twice -> still one rule; an answer with record false -> no rule; a decision of kind 'rule' answered with record true -> no rule; a decision answered with record true before the service exists -> svc.Start() stores its rule}: assert svc.Rules() and each rule's fields; for the rows without a rule assert the fake hub saw no request to a forks route and the session fake was not asked

criteria.condition: a decision is answered without `record`, or a decision of kind `rule` is answered with `record: true`
criteria.action: store no rule, create no fork and ask for no session for that answer
criteria.contract: no rule exists for the decision; the hub received no request to `POST …/forks`; no session was asked for

criteria.condition: a rule is in the state `writing`, no session of it runs, and the hub is available to the worker credential
criteria.action: create the fork `<slug>--rule-<decision id>` with `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/forks` (`name: "rule-<decision id>"`, `auto_change: false`), taking `409 conflict` as the fork being there already; choose the rule's target where it has none (`adr` when `GET …/scm/tree` of the fork with `path=docs/adr` lists at least one entry, else `steering` when `GET …/scm/file` with `path=.specs/steering.md` answers 200, else `decisions`); and ask the scheduler for a planner session with no item, the scope `{the rule's workspace, the rule's thread, the key rule-<decision id>}`, the step `rule`, the fork, and the branch `rule-<decision id>-<n>`, n being one more than the number of branches the rule discarded
criteria.contract: the hub received one fork request with that name and `auto_change: false`; the session request has `Role: planner`, `Item: 0`, the scope, the fork and the branch; its prompt names the target and holds `{input:rule}` and `{result}`; the input `rule` is the JSON object {decision, kind, question, answer, comment, target}; a target once chosen is the target of every later session of the rule

setup: the workspace `demo` on the fake hub with a git repository whose content the row sets
a rule in `writing` for decision 5 of the test kind
check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/rule_test.go, a table over the fork's tree {docs/adr/01-x.md present -> target 'adr'; no docs/adr but .specs/steering.md -> 'steering'; neither -> 'decisions'}: svc.Pass(ctx); assert fakeHub.Forks('demo') == ['demo--rule-5'] created with auto_change false; req = sessions.Asked()[0]; assert req.Role == planner and req.Item == 0 and req.Scope == {demo, thread, 'rule-5'} and req.Step == 'rule' and req.Fork == 'demo--rule-5' and req.Branch == 'rule-5-1'; assert json(req.Inputs['rule']) == {decision: 5, kind: 'test', question, answer: 'yes', comment, target}; assert req.Prompt contains '{input:rule}' and '{result}'. A second service over the same store and a fake hub that answers the fork request 409 conflict: assert one session asked for the same fork and no error

criteria.condition: a rule's session ends `completed`, and `GET /api/v1/workspaces/{fork}/scm/diff` with `base` the fork's default branch and `head` the session's branch lists exactly the one file the rule's target allows: for `adr` a file with `status: added` directly in `docs/adr/`; for `steering` the file `.specs/steering.md` with `status: modified`, `deletions: 0` and no unchanged line after the first added line of its patch; for `decisions` a file with `status: added` under `docs/decisions/`
criteria.action: open the rule's change, where it has none, with `POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes` (the fork and the branch as `source`, the title `Rule: <the question, cut to 80 characters>`, the intent `Recorded from decision <id>: <question>`, not a draft); set the rule to `proposed` with the change's number and version; and open a decision of kind `rule` in the rule's thread with the question `Add this rule to <slug>?`, the evidence `rule` (the added lines of the file's patch without their leading `+`), `file` (the file's path) and `change` (`<slug>#<number>`), the option `approve` recommended and `nothing` as what it blocks
criteria.contract: the kind `rule` is declared with the options `approve`, `revise` (comment required) and `discard`; the decision is open in the rule's thread; the rule has exactly one change on the hub; the rule's state is `proposed`

setup: the fake hub serving scm/diff from the fork's repository
check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/rule_test.go, a table over {target adr, the scripted session pushes a commit adding docs/adr/02-never-cache.md with the text T; target steering, the commit appends two lines to .specs/steering.md; target decisions, the commit adds docs/decisions/never-cache.md}: svc.Pass(ctx) until the rule is 'proposed'; ch = fakeHub.Changes('demo')[0]; assert ch.source == {demo--rule-5, rule-5-1} and ch.draft == false and ch.title == 'Rule: ' + question; d = inbox.OpenDecisions()[0]; assert d.Kind == 'rule' and d.Question == 'Add this rule to demo?' and d.Blocks == 'nothing'; assert d.Evidence == [{rule, the added text}, {file, the path}, {change, 'demo#' + ch.number}]; assert d.Options keys == ['approve','revise','discard'] with approve recommended and revise comment_required

criteria.condition: a rule's session ends `failed`, or ends `completed` while the diff of its branch lists no file, a file the rule's target does not allow, or the allowed file with another status or, for `steering`, with a removed line or an unchanged line after an added one
criteria.action: count one failed session in a row for the rule, open no change for that branch, and, when it is the first failure in a row, ask for the session again: on the next branch for a rule without a change, on the same branch for a rule with one
criteria.contract: the failure's reason is the session's own reason, `no rule written` for a diff without a file, `rule change touches <path>` for the first file in order of path that the target does not allow, or `rule change alters <path>` for the allowed file in a form the target does not allow; the hub received no `POST …/changes` for the branch; the rule stays `writing`; a session that completes with an allowed change sets the count to zero

check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/rule_test.go, a table over the first session of a rule with target adr {outcome failed with reason 'stalled' -> 'stalled'; completed with no commit -> 'no rule written'; a commit adding docs/adr/02-x.md and README.md -> 'rule change touches README.md'; a commit modifying docs/adr/01-x.md -> 'rule change alters docs/adr/01-x.md'} and with target steering {a commit that deletes a line of .specs/steering.md -> 'rule change alters .specs/steering.md'; a commit that inserts a line in the middle -> the same}: svc.Pass(ctx); assert rule.Failures == [reason]; assert rule.State == 'writing'; assert fakeHub.Changes('demo') is empty; assert the second session asked has Branch 'rule-5-2'. One more row: the first session ends 'interrupted' -> rule.Failures is empty and the second session has Branch 'rule-5-1'. One row over a restart: a rule left in 'writing' by a closed service -> the new service asks one session on the same branch

criteria.condition: a rule's session fails for the second time in a row
criteria.action: set the rule to `failed`, abandon its change where it has one, append to the rule's thread one entry of kind `rule_failed` with the text `rule for decision <id> not written: <first reason>; <second reason>`, marking the thread unread, and ask for no further session of the rule
criteria.contract: the rule's state is `failed`; the thread holds exactly one `rule_failed` entry and is unread; no decision was opened; a later pass asks for no session

check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/rule_test.go: two scripted sessions, the first 'stalled', the second completing with a commit that adds README.md; svc.Pass(ctx) twice; assert rule.State == 'failed'; assert the thread's last entry == {kind: 'rule_failed', text: 'rule for decision 5 not written: stalled; rule change touches README.md'} and thread.unread; assert inbox.OpenDecisions() is empty; svc.Pass(ctx); assert sessions.Asked() has 2 requests. A rule with a change (after a revise) failing twice: assert the fake hub saw POST …/changes/<n>/abandon

criteria.condition: a rule's session ends `interrupted`, or nightshiftd starts with a rule in the state `writing`
criteria.action: ask for the rule's session again on the same branch and count no failure

requirements.title: The rule decision: approve, land and publish, revise, discard
requirements.rationale: A rule binds later sessions, so its text lands only when the person approved it, and then goes the way of every other change.

criteria.condition: a `rule` decision was answered `approve`, the rule's workspace is `green`, its pause flag is not set, the hub is available to the worker credential, and the sync from origin that precedes any landing, run through package 08's `publish.Service.Sync(ctx, slug)`, returned no error
criteria.action: report the checks `nightshift-gate`, `nightshift-review` and `nightshift-release` with `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/changes/{number}/checks/{name}` as `passed` on the change's current version with the summary `rule approved by the owner`, through the hub client's `ReportCheck`, and then ask the hub to land the change through package 07's `land.Service.LandChange(ctx, Request{Workspace, Change, Version})`, which sends `POST …/changes/{number}/land` with that version as `expected_version`
criteria.contract: the hub received the three check reports, each with `status: passed`, the version and the summary, before one land request carrying `expected_version`; no approval was recorded and no `override` was sent; the rule was `approved` from the answer on

setup: a rule in `proposed` with change n at version 1 and its open `rule` decision d, the workspace `demo` green

the rule service is given four functions at its creation: the sync (`publish.Service.Sync`), the land (`land.Service.LandChange`, here the real one over the fake hub), the health check (`health.Service.VerifyTip`) and the push (`publish.Service.PushTip`); here the sync, the health check and the push are recording fakes that pass
check.pseudocode: new file internal/rule/land_test.go: inbox.Answer(ctx, d.ID, {Option: 'approve'}); svc.Pass(ctx); assert fakeHub.Checks('demo', n) == {nightshift-gate, nightshift-review, nightshift-release} each {status: 'passed', version: 1, summary: 'rule approved by the owner'}; assert the fake hub's request log has the three PUTs before one POST …/land with body {expected_version: 1}; assert fakeHub.Approvals('demo', n) is empty

criteria.condition: a rule is `approved` and its workspace is `red` or `held`, or the workspace's pause flag is set, or the hub is not available to the worker credential, or `publish.Service.Sync` returned an error for the sync before the landing
criteria.action: report no check and send no land request for the rule, keep it `approved`, and carry out REQ-2.1 at the first pass at which none of these holds

check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/land_test.go, a table over {workspace state red; workspace state held; workspace paused; hub.Available(worker) false; the sync function returns an error}: answer approve; svc.Pass(ctx) three times; assert the fake hub saw no PUT …/checks and no POST …/land; assert rule.State == 'approved'; lift the condition; svc.Pass(ctx); assert one land request

criteria.condition: `LandChange` returns an `Outcome` of the kind `landed` for a rule's change
criteria.action: set the rule to `landed` with the outcome's `LandedSHA`; append to the rule's thread the entry `rule_landed` with the text `rule for decision <id> landed as <sha>`; run the workspace's health command on that commit through package 08's `health.Service.VerifyTip(ctx, slug, commit)`, its check of a commit no item is to blame for; when that returns nil, push the workspace's default branch to origin through `publish.Service.PushTip(ctx, slug)` (REQ-6.4); and when that reports the branch on origin, set the rule to `published` and append the entry `rule_published` with the text `rule for decision <id> is on origin`
criteria.contract: `VerifyTip` was called once with the workspace and the landed commit, and `PushTip` once after it returned nil; the rule's state is `published`; neither entry marks the thread unread

check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/land_test.go: the fake hub lands change n as sha S; answer approve; svc.Pass(ctx) until rule.State == 'published'; assert health.calls == [{demo, S}] and push.calls == [demo], in that order; assert the thread's entries end with {rule_landed, 'rule for decision 5 landed as ' + S}, {rule_published, 'rule for decision 5 is on origin'}; assert thread.unread is as it was before the pass

criteria.condition: `LandChange` returns for a rule's change an `Outcome` of a kind other than `landed` (`pending_approval`, `pending`, `blocked`, `conflict`, `version_mismatch` or `failed`)
criteria.action: set the rule to `failed`, abandon the change, and append to the rule's thread one entry of kind `rule_failed` with the text `rule for decision <id> not landed: <the outcome's kind>`, followed by `: <reason>` where the outcome has a reason, marking the thread unread
criteria.contract: the rule's state is `failed`; the hub received `POST …/changes/{number}/abandon`; no decision of kind `approval`, `conflict` or `blocked` was opened and no session was asked for; the health and publish functions were not called

check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/land_test.go, a table over the land's scripted answer and the text after 'not landed: ' {409 land_conflict -> 'conflict'; 409 policy_blocked whose requirement lacks an approval -> 'pending_approval'; 409 policy_blocked with blocked.status blocked -> 'blocked'; 409 version_mismatch -> 'version_mismatch'; 503 land_failed with error timeout -> 'failed: land_failed: timeout'}: answer approve; svc.Pass(ctx); assert rule.State == 'failed'; assert the thread's last entry == {rule_failed, 'rule for decision 5 not landed: ' + text} and thread.unread; assert the fake hub saw one POST …/land; assert fakeHub.Change('demo', n).state == 'abandoned'; assert inbox.OpenDecisions() is empty; assert health.calls and push.calls are empty

criteria.condition: `VerifyTip` returns an error for a rule's landed commit, or `PushTip` does not report the branch on origin
criteria.action: leave the rule `landed`, call neither function for it a second time, and open no decision and ask for no session of its own
criteria.contract: the rule's state stays `landed`; the thread has a `rule_landed` entry and no `rule_published` entry; `PushTip` was not called after `VerifyTip` returned an error; what `VerifyTip` did for the failure (the workspace `red`, the `main_red` decision in the workspace's thread) is as package 08 specifies it

check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/land_test.go, a table over {the health fake returns an error -> push.calls is empty; the health fake returns nil and the push fake returns false}: answer approve; svc.Pass(ctx) three times; assert rule.State == 'landed'; assert no entry of kind rule_published; assert health.calls has length 1; assert inbox.OpenDecisions() is empty

criteria.condition: a `rule` decision is answered `revise` with its comment
criteria.action: set the rule to `writing` and ask for its session again on the branch of its change, with the comment as the further input `comment`; and when that session's branch passes the check of REQ-1.4, open a new `rule` decision for the change's new version
criteria.contract: the change keeps its number and has a version one higher; the answered decision stays answered; the new decision's evidence `rule` shows the new text; the checks of an approval are then reported on the new version

check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/land_test.go: inbox.Answer(ctx, d.ID, {Option: 'revise', Comment: 'shorter'}); the scripted session pushes a second commit to rule-5-1 that rewrites the added file; svc.Pass(ctx) until 'proposed'; req = sessions.Asked()[1]; assert req.Branch == 'rule-5-1' and req.Inputs['comment'] == 'shorter'; assert len(fakeHub.Changes('demo')) == 1 and its version == 2; d2 = inbox.OpenDecisions()[0]; assert d2.ID != d.ID and d2.Evidence[0].Text == the new text; answer d2 approve; svc.Pass(ctx); assert every check report has version 2. An answer 'revise' without a comment through POST /api/v1/decisions/{id}/answer -> 400 comment_required

criteria.condition: a `rule` decision is answered `discard`
criteria.action: abandon the rule's change with `POST …/changes/{number}/abandon`, set the rule to `discarded`, and append to the rule's thread the entry `rule_discarded` with the text `rule for decision <id> discarded`
criteria.contract: the change's state on the hub is `abandoned`; the rule's state is `discarded`; no check was reported and no land was asked for; a later pass does nothing for the rule

check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/land_test.go: inbox.Answer(ctx, d.ID, {Option: 'discard'}); svc.Pass(ctx); assert fakeHub.Change('demo', n).state == 'abandoned'; assert rule.State == 'discarded'; assert the thread's last entry == {rule_discarded, 'rule for decision 5 discarded'}; assert no PUT …/checks and no POST …/land in the request log

criteria.action: for any answer to a `rule` decision whose handler is called more than once, and for any rule found `approved` or `landed` when nightshiftd starts, carry out the answer's effect once: one report of each check for a version, one landing, one call of `VerifyTip` and of `PushTip`, one abandon; taking a change the hub reports as `landed` as landed, and one it reports as `abandoned` as abandoned

check.pseudocode: in internal/rule/land_test.go, a table over {the approve handler called twice -> one land request; a service closed after the land answered 200 and before the rule was stored as landed, then a new service over the same store -> no second land request, GET …/changes/{n} read, rule 'published', health.calls has length 1; the discard handler called twice with the hub answering the second abandon 409 change_closed -> rule 'discarded' and one rule_discarded entry; a handler called for a decision whose rule is no longer 'proposed' -> nothing changes}

requirements.title: The outcome numbers and nightshift stats
requirements.rationale: Whether unattended work goes well shows in a few numbers over weeks, not in any one thread.

criteria.condition: an authenticated client requests `GET /api/v1/stats`, optionally with `workspace=<slug>` naming a registered workspace and `days=<N>` from 1 to 365 (30 when absent)
criteria.action: answer, for the named workspace or for every registered workspace in order of slug, the outcome numbers over the N times 24 hours before the request, with `done` and `abandoned` being the numbers of the workspace's items in that state whose `state_since` lies in that time
criteria.contract: status 200 with `{"days": N, "workspaces": [{"workspace", "done", "abandoned", "first_pass", "sessions_per_item", "reverted", "taken_over", "decisions_per_done_item", "decision_wait_seconds", "creation_to_done_seconds", "tokens_per_done_item"}]}`; `done`, `abandoned`, `reverted` and `taken_over` are integers and 0 when nothing is counted

setup: a helper in internal/stats that seeds one store: clock now = T; workspace `demo` with item A (created T-27h, done T-23h; sessions planner completed 100 tokens, implementer completed 1000, reviewer completed 200; one decision opened T-27h and answered T-25h), item B (created T-3d, done T-2d; sessions implementer failed 50, implementer completed 500, reviewer completed 100, a second implementer completed 300 that started after the first completed one ended, reviewer completed 100; two decisions with waits of 1h and 3h answered at T-60h and T-50h; a `state` entry `verifying -> awaiting_approval` at T-53h and a `taken_over` entry at T-51h), item C (abandoned at T-3d), item D (done at T-40d with one implementer session of 9000 tokens), item E (ready, never done); and workspace `empty` with no item
check.pseudocode: new file internal/stats/stats_test.go, one table over (workspace, days) with the whole expected object: {demo, 30 -> done 2, abandoned 1, first_pass 50, sessions_per_item 4, reverted 1, taken_over 1, decisions_per_done_item 1.5, decision_wait_seconds 7200, creation_to_done_seconds 50400, tokens_per_done_item 1175; demo, 1 -> done 1, abandoned 0, first_pass 100, sessions_per_item 3, reverted 0, taken_over 0, decisions_per_done_item 1, decision_wait_seconds null, creation_to_done_seconds 14400, tokens_per_done_item 1300; demo, 365 -> done 3; empty, 30 -> the four counts 0 and the six other members null}: got = stats.Compute(ctx, slug, days); assert got == want. In new file internal/stats/routes_test.go through the router: get('/api/v1/stats') -> 200, days 30 and the workspaces [demo, empty] in that order; get('/api/v1/stats?workspace=demo&days=1') -> one workspace equal to the table's row

criteria.action: for any workspace and time asked for, answer `first_pass` as the share, in whole percent rounded to the nearest, of the items that reached `done` in that time for which no implementer session started after the end of the item's first implementer session with the status `completed`, and `sessions_per_item` as the median, over those items, of the number of sessions recorded for the item, of every role and status, a median of an even number of values being the mean of the two in the middle

for any workspace and time asked for, answer `reverted` as the number of the workspace's items whose thread holds, with a time in that time, an entry of kind `state` whose text begins `verifying -> awaiting_approval`, and `taken_over` as the number of its items whose thread holds, with a time in that time, an entry of kind `taken_over`, each item counted once

for any workspace and time asked for, answer `decisions_per_done_item` as the number of answered decisions in the threads of the items that reached `done` in that time divided by the number of those items, rounded to one decimal, and `decision_wait_seconds` as the median, over the decisions of the workspace's threads that were answered in that time, of the seconds from the decision's opening to its answer

for any workspace and time asked for, answer `creation_to_done_seconds` as the median, over the items that reached `done` in that time, of the seconds from the item's `created_at` to its `state_since`, and `tokens_per_done_item` as the median, over those items, of the sum of the tokens of the item's recorded sessions

for any workspace in which no item reached `done` in the time asked for, answer `first_pass`, `sessions_per_item`, `decisions_per_done_item`, `creation_to_done_seconds` and `tokens_per_done_item` as null, and for any workspace in which no decision was answered in that time, answer `decision_wait_seconds` as null

criteria.condition: the person runs `nightshift stats [<slug>] [--days <N>]`
criteria.action: request `GET /api/v1/stats` with the slug as `workspace` and N as `days`, each only when given, and print for each workspace the line `<slug>, last <N> days` and then, indented by two spaces, the lines `done <n>, abandoned <n>`, `first pass <n>%, sessions per item <n>`, `reverted <n>, taken over <n>`, `decisions per done item <n>, decision wait <duration>`, `creation to done <duration>` and `tokens per done item <n>`, a null printed as `-` (without the `%`), a duration as `<d>d <h>h` from 24 hours on, `<h>h <m>m` from one hour on and `<m>m` below, rounded down, and a number without a fraction printed without a decimal point
criteria.contract: exit code 0; the lines on stdout; with `--json` stdout is the API's JSON

setup: an httptest server standing in for the daemon
check.pseudocode:
in internal/cli/cli_test.go (package 01's file), a table over the served document {the demo row of 30 days -> 'demo, last 30 days
  done 2, abandoned 1
  first pass 50%, sessions per item 4
  reverted 1, taken over 1
  decisions per done item 1.5, decision wait 2h 0m
  creation to done 14h 0m
  tokens per done item 1175
'; the empty row -> '  first pass -, sessions per item -' and 'decision wait -' among its lines; a wait of 93600 seconds -> '1d 2h'; a wait of 540 seconds -> '9m'; --json -> stdout parses to the served document}: code, stdout, _ = cli.Run(['stats', 'demo', '--days', '30', …]); assert code == 0; assert stdout; assert the httptest server saw GET /api/v1/stats?days=30&workspace=demo; cli.Run(['stats']) -> the request has no query

criteria.condition: `nightshift stats` is given a `--days` that is not a decimal integer from 1 to 365, a second slug or an unknown flag; or a request to `GET /api/v1/stats` carries such a `days`, or names a workspace that is not registered
criteria.action: refuse the command without sending a request, and refuse the request without computing anything
criteria.contract: the client: exit code 2, the usage of `stats` on stderr, stdout empty, no request sent; the API: status 400 with `error_type: invalid_request` for `days`, status 404 with `error_type: not_found` for the workspace

check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/cli_test.go, a table over {['stats','--days','0'], ['stats','--days','366'], ['stats','--days','x'], ['stats','a','b']}: assert code == 2 and stderr contains 'usage: nightshift stats' and the httptest server saw no request. In internal/stats/routes_test.go, a table over {days=0, days=366, days=1.5, days=abc -> 400 invalid_request; workspace=nope -> 404 not_found}: assert r.status and r.json.error_type

requirements.title: The daily brief and nightshift brief
requirements.rationale: A person who does not watch needs one place, once a day, that says what finished, what waits for them and what it cost.

criteria.condition: the time in the daemon's time zone reaches `brief.at` (`08:00` unless configured) on a day for which no brief was made yet, and since the previous brief an item of any workspace was created or changed its state, or a decision is open
criteria.action: append one entry of kind `brief` to the installation's brief thread, marking the thread unread, whose text is the brief for the period from the time of the thread's last `brief` entry, or from 24 hours before when it has none, to that moment; record the local day as made; and call `Notify` of `internal/notify` with the event `brief` and the brief thread's URL path
criteria.contract: the brief thread gains exactly one entry and is in the view `unread`; one notification was sent whose document has `event: "brief"`, `time` and `thread`, and neither `workspace` nor `item`; the entry's text begins `brief <since> to <until>` with both times in RFC 3339 UTC

setup: a brief runner over a copy of the store template, the inbox, the item service and a recording notifier
check.pseudocode: new file internal/brief/daily_test.go, with an injected clock in a zone two hours east of UTC and `brief.at` 08:00, the runner's check driven by the test: one item created yesterday; clock = 07:59 local; r.Check(ctx); assert the brief thread has no entry; clock = 08:00; r.Check(ctx); assert one entry {kind: 'brief'} whose text starts 'brief ' + (until - 24h) + ' to ' + until, thread.unread, and notifier.events == [{brief, thread: '/api/v1/threads/<id>'}] without workspace and item; clock = 09:00; r.Check(ctx); assert still one entry (one a day). Next day with nothing changed and no open decision: r.Check at 08:00 -> no new entry, no notification, and a second r.Check at 10:00 after an item was created -> still no new entry that day. The day after: r.Check at 08:00 -> a second entry whose period starts at the first entry's time. A runner created at 11:00 local over a store with no brief made that day -> its first Check writes the brief; a runner created at 11:00 on a day already recorded -> writes none; a store whose last made day is three days back -> one entry, not three

execution_paths.title: A recorded answer becomes a rule on origin

steps.action: answers a decision of workspace `demo` with `nightshift decide <id> --option yes --comment "Never cache greetings" --record`
stores a rule for the decision, creates the fork `demo--rule-<id>` on the hub, finds `docs/adr/` in it and starts a planner session with no item on the branch `rule-<id>-1`
adds one file under `docs/adr/` holding the question, the answer and the comment, pushes the branch to the fork and writes its result file
answers the diff of the branch with the one added file
opens the change and a `rule` decision that shows the file's text
runs `nightshift decide <rule decision> --option approve`
syncs from origin, reports the three checks as passed with `rule approved by the owner` and asks the hub to land the version
lands the change on the default branch
runs the health command on the landed commit and asks the hub to push the default branch
receives the default branch with the new file

the hub client of internal/hub against the fake hub's fork, source control, change, check, land and push routes and its git endpoint
a planner session started through the session helper

symbols.name: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/forks
symbols.signature: scope workspaces:write; body {name?: 1-32 of a-z, digits, hyphens, ref?, ttl?: e.g. "7d", auto_change?: bool (default true), purpose?, session_id?, token?}; the fork's slug is <parent>--<name>; 201 {workspace, remote, token?}; 409 conflict when the parent has a fork of that name; 400 invalid_request, 400 not_supported_on_fork, 429 fork_limit_reached

symbols.signature: scope git:read; query ref? (default the default branch), path? (default the root), recursive?; 200 a list of entries {path, name, type: blob|tree|symlink|commit, mode, sha, size}; 400 invalid_request for a path that names a file

symbols.name: GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/scm/file
symbols.signature: query path (required), ref? (default the default branch); 200 the file's bytes, or with Accept: application/json {path, sha, mode, size, encoding, content, resolved_sha}; 404 path_not_found; 400 invalid_request for a directory

symbols.name: GET /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/scm/diff
symbols.signature: query base, head (both required), mode? merge_base (default) | direct, path?, patches? (default true), context? 0-20 (default 3), format? json; 200 {base_sha, head_sha, merge_base_sha, files: [{path, old_path, status: added|modified|deleted|renamed|copied|type_changed, insertions, deletions, binary, old_sha, new_sha, patch}], stats, truncated}

symbols.name: POST /api/v1/workspaces/{slug}/issues/{number}/comments
